about: What lib/precompile.mjs turns EXEC CICS into, and the IBM documents that say so: for each command it translates, each option's argument type and the direction its data moves, which decides whether the CALL passes it BY CONTENT or BY REFERENCE; the numbers DFHRESP and DFHVALUE stand for; and what the translator adds to the LINKAGE SECTION. lib/cics-commands.mjs is generated from this file and provenance/words.json by diag/generate-precompile.mjs, and test/precompile.test.mjs checks that the two agree. The directions and notes are this project's reading of the documents, written in its own words; no text, copybook or translator output of IBM's is reproduced beyond names and numbers.
method: Each command's options and argument types were read from its syntax diagram in the CICS TS 5.3 Application Programming Reference (rendered to text with macOS PDFKit); every option-with-argument in the diagram is listed. The reference defines the argument types: a data-value only sends, a data-area receives and also sends where the option's description says so (FROM is its example), a ptr-ref receives, and a name, filename, systemname, hhmmss or ptr-value is given to CICS. Each data-area option's description was read, and one that sends, or sends and receives, carries a note saying why, with the page where the manual says so; a note without a page is an input the description names as the thing the command acts on or writes out. A cvda option's direction is read from its command: ASSIGN returns them, every other listed command is given them. 'identify' and 'default' are this project's rules for telling a command from its namesakes (SEND MAP from SEND), not IBM's. The URL in 'doc' is the command's page in IBM's current CICS TS documentation, for a reader; the facts were read from the 5.3 manuals, whose files are hashed below.
docsChecked: 2026-09-28: each command's 'doc' page was fetched and its title read as EXEC CICS and the command's name.

linkage.fact: By default the translator makes sure each program's LINKAGE SECTION, which it creates when there is none, declares DFHEIBLK and DFHCOMMAREA, and adds USING DFHEIBLK DFHCOMMAREA to a top-level program's PROCEDURE DIVISION header when it has no USING; a nested program also gets a DATA DIVISION when it has none, and its header is left alone.
linkage.here: COPY DFHEIBLK goes after the LINKAGE SECTION header, or before the PROCEDURE DIVISION header under a LINKAGE SECTION (and DATA DIVISION) added for it, in each program unit with CICS in it or naming an EIB field, unless the unit declares DFHEIBLK itself. 01 DFHCOMMAREA PIC X goes with it only where the unit names DFHCOMMAREA without declaring it: a declaration nothing names changes nothing a compiler or reader sees. The one-byte size is this project's choice; the guide gives none. The PROCEDURE DIVISION header is left as written: a compiler needs no USING to accept a program that names a LINKAGE item.

handle.fact: HANDLE CONDITION takes effect when it runs, not where it is written: from then on a condition a later command raises passes control to the label named for it, or for ERROR, until an IGNORE CONDITION or another HANDLE CONDITION for the same condition runs. A command with RESP or NOHANDLE is exempt, the handling is suspended while control is in a program this one LINKs or XCTLs to, and PUSH HANDLE and POP HANDLE save and restore it. For HANDLE ABEND LABEL in COBOL the reference says control returns to the HANDLE ABEND command and a COBOL GO TO then runs.

secondary.title: M. G. J. van den Brand, M. P. A. Sellink, C. Verhoef, Control Flow Normalization for COBOL/CICS Legacy Systems (1997), section 7
secondary.says: the translator follows the CALL for a HANDLE with SERVICE LABEL and a GO TO ... DEPENDING ON DFHEIGDI over the HANDLE's labels

secondary.title: M. P. A. Sellink, H. M. Sneed, C. Verhoef, Restructuring of COBOL/CICS Legacy Systems
secondary.says: the same shape for HANDLE ABEND, HANDLE CONDITION and HANDLE AID, one target per labelled option in the order written

marks.HANDLE ABEND LABEL: documented that control returns to the HANDLE and a GO TO runs; the DEPENDING ON form is secondary
marks.HANDLE CONDITION: secondary, and inferred from HANDLE ABEND
marks.HANDLE AID: secondary, and inferred from HANDLE ABEND

handle.here: Each HANDLE CONDITION, HANDLE AID and HANDLE ABEND LABEL becomes its CALL followed by GO TO over its labels, in the order written, DEPENDING ON DFHEIGDI, which the EIB stand-in declares. When the HANDLE runs DFHEIGDI is 0 and control falls through; the branch is taken when CICS returns there. SERVICE LABEL, which IBM's translators put between the two, is left out: GnuCOBOL 3.2 refuses it. Which later command sends control back follows execution order, and is the control model's to draw; nothing is added after the commands themselves. Unobserved: no IBM translator has been run.
